land.text: the whole archipelago, the Anglo-French Condominium of the New Hebrides: 'The New Hebrides, now renamed Vanuatu, achieved independence as planned on 30 July 1980'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's New Hebrides row runs 1890-1982 and its Vanuatu row starts 1983; the oc-02-a New Hebrides dossier cuts the colony at 30 July 1980. The infobox gives independence 'from the United Kingdom and France'. Matthew and Hunter are 'claimed and controlled by France'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Vanuatu row starts 1983 and leaves 1980-1982 to its New Hebrides row, but independence was 30 July 1980 (infobox 'from the United Kingdom and France: 30 July 1980'). Espiritu Santo was in rebel hands from before independence to 28 August 1980 (ledger contest events).

correction.text: all six provinces the page names, from the Torres and Banks Islands (Torba) to Tanna, Futuna, Erromango and Aneityum (Tafea)

keyframe_review.note: 16,885 km2 against the infobox 12,189 km2 (ratio 1.39, within a factor of two; the body text says 12,274). The outline is simplified: at the gazetteer's grid it holds 28 land cells against 43 for the country polygon and ends at 18.87S, leaving out cells in Sanma (4), Penama (3), Tafea (3), Malampa (2), Shefa (2) and Torba (2). The country spec draws every island the page lists.

ledger.note: 1980: the New Hebrides become the independent Republic of Vanuatu. 'The New Hebrides, now renamed Vanuatu, achieved independence as planned on 30 July 1980'; infobox 'from the United Kingdom and France: 30 July 1980'.

region.text: Espiritu Santo (Sanma province includes Santo and Malo)

ledger.note: 1980: Espiritu Santo is held by secessionists as Vanuatu becomes independent. 'Beginning in June 1980, Jimmy Stevens, head of the Nagriamel movement, led an uprising'; the rebels 'declared the independence of Espiritu Santo island as the "State of Vemerana"'; the conflict occurred 'shortly before and after' 30 July 1980. The month is the researcher's reading (independence day); the Vanuatu page, as read, says the secessionists 'took over the island's government in January' and calls it the 'Republic of Vemarana'.

region.text: Espiritu Santo (Sanma province includes Santo and Malo)

ledger.note: 1980: the Santo secession ends. Stevens surrendered on 28 August 1980 and 'the war came to a sudden end'; Papua New Guinean soldiers had been sent at Walter Lini's request. The Vanuatu page says Stevens 'surrendered on 1 September'.

wars.name: Coconut War

zones.text: Espiritu Santo (Sanma province includes Santo and Malo)

wars.outcome: Government victory: the Nagriamel secession on Espiritu Santo, which lasted 'about 12 weeks', ended with Stevens's surrender on 28 August 1980; the infobox lists a 'Vanuatuan, Papua New Guinean and Solomon Islander victory'.
wars.note: The rebels were supported by French-speaking residents and the Phoenix Foundation. The Vanuatu page says British and French troops were sent in July 1980 and Lini then called in Papua New Guinean troops. The rebel state held land for about three months, so no rebel-type dossier is proposed.

certainty.note: Island coasts; maritime limits are not drawn. Matthew and Hunter are 'claimed and controlled by France' and are outside the shape.

notes: Cliopatria rows. The Vanuatu row starts 1983 although independence was 30 July 1980 (a 1980-1982 keyframe is added); the New Hebrides row (oc-02-a) is cut at 30 July 1980 in that dossier. The outline misses cells of every province at the grid's resolution (see the 1983 verdict). The Santo secession (State of Vemerana, called 'Republic of Vemarana' on the Vanuatu page) held Espiritu Santo for about 12 weeks around independence; it is recorded as a contest, not as a rebel dossier. The declaration date is not on either page (the Vanuatu page says 'in January', the Coconut War page 'beginning in June 1980'), and the end is 28 August (Coconut War) or 1 September (Vanuatu). The Matthew and Hunter dispute has no date on the page, so there is no event for it. Pre-state: the 1887 Joint Naval Commission, the 1906 Condominium and the 1914 Protocol are the New Hebrides dossier's.
